analysis.title: Strategic: Navigate transformational innovation
key_insights: UBS CIO sees three long-term growth areas driven by technological innovation and structural change: AI, power and resources, and longevity.
UBS expects AI investment to keep rising in 2027, supported by demand for computing capacity, cloud growth, and expanding usage as costs fall.

UBS says future AI returns are uncertain. It expects periods of excess capacity, weaker pricing, and doubts about profitability, and notes that in parts of the industry investment already runs ahead of revenue.

UBS lists rising financing costs, execution challenges, power shortages, and data center constraints as AI risks. Slower cloud growth, weaker business adoption, or supply overtaking demand could further undermine confidence.

UBS recommends retaining AI exposure and preparing for volatility. It favors financially strong hyperscalers with visible monetization and internally funded investment, plus select leaders in compute, foundry, and semiconductor equipment.

In key developed markets, electricity demand net of efficiency gains is rising for the first time in decades. AI competes with electrification, grid modernization, EVs, industrial automation, and the energy transition for power and equipment.
UBS projects USD 32tr of global electrical infrastructure spending over the next decade, covering power generation, grids, storage, and critical minerals.

UBS sees the best power opportunities where supply constraints are tightest: companies with scarce production capacity, established order books, strong customer relationships, and a record of delivering complex projects.

UBS advises selectivity in power and resources at this stage of the cycle. It monitors rising financing rates, input cost inflation, permitting delays, and the pace of data center construction, but believes the size and duration of the cycle will exceed what the market currently appreciates.
UBS expects the longevity economy to grow around 6% a year to USD 8tr by 2030, driven by aging populations and advances in drug discovery, diagnostics, and medical technology.

UBS forecasts global obesity treatment revenues to grow an average of 12% a year through 2030, helped by more manufacturing capacity, lower prices, oral treatments, wider reimbursement, and additional clinical indications.

UBS says health care has a different earnings profile from AI infrastructure and other capital-intensive industries, with demand generally less sensitive to the economic cycle. Individual stocks remain exposed to clinical results, regulation, and patent expiries.

sector_views.rationale: Retain AI exposure. Favors strong hyperscalers with internally funded investment and select leaders in compute, foundry, and semiconductor equipment, while preparing for volatility.
Favors suppliers with scarce capacity, order books, and pricing power, with selectivity on end-markets and competitive moat.
Aging populations and medical innovation support growth, including obesity treatment revenues growing 12% a year through 2030, with less cyclical demand.

risk_factors: AI investment running ahead of revenue in parts of the industry, with rising financing costs, execution challenges, power shortages, and data center constraints.
Slower cloud growth, weaker business adoption, or supply overtaking demand in AI.
Power and resources risks: rising financing rates, input cost inflation, permitting delays, and the pace of data center construction.
Health care risks: clinical results, regulation, and patent expiries.
